draft.title: Magnitude and unit vectors
card: The magnitude of a vector is its length. It is written |v|. For v = ai + bj, |v| = √(a² + b²), from Pythagoras' theorem.
Example: for v = 3i − 4j, |v| = √(3² + (−4)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. Squaring removes the minus sign.
a vector with magnitude 1. It shows direction only.
To find the unit vector in the direction of v, divide v by |v|. For v = 3i − 4j, the unit vector is (3/5)i − (4/5)j.
draft.remember: Magnitude is √(a² + b²). Divide a vector by its magnitude to get a unit vector.

a.q: What is the magnitude of the vector 5i − 12j?
a.why: |v| = √(5² + (−12)²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. Adding 5 and 12 to get 17 skips the squaring and the square root. A magnitude is a length, so it is never negative.
a.clue: Square each component, add, then take the square root.

b.q: Which is the unit vector in the same direction as 6i + 8j?
b.why: |6i + 8j| = √(36 + 64) = 10, so divide each component by 10 to get (3/5)i + (4/5)j. Check: (3/5)² + (4/5)² = 9/25 + 16/25 = 1. Dividing by 14, the sum of the components, gives (3/7)i + (4/7)j, which has magnitude less than 1.
b.clue: Find the magnitude first, then divide both components by it.

final.title: Magnitude and unit vectors
card: The magnitude of a vector is its length. It is written \(|v|\). For \(v = ai + bj\), \(|v| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\), from Pythagoras' theorem.
Example: for \(v = 3i - 4j\), \(|v| = \sqrt{3^{2} + (-4)^{2}}\) \(= \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\). Squaring removes the minus sign.
a vector with magnitude 1. It shows direction only.
To find the unit vector in the direction of \(v\), divide \(v\) by \(|v|\). For \(v = 3i - 4j\), the unit vector is \(\frac{3}{5}i - \frac{4}{5}j\).
final.remember: Magnitude is \(\sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\). Divide a vector by its magnitude to get a unit vector.

a.q: What is the magnitude of the vector \(5i - 12j\)?
a.why: \(|v| = \sqrt{5^{2} + (-12)^{2}}\) \(= \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13\). Adding 5 and 12 to get 17 skips the squaring and the square root. A magnitude is a length, so it is never negative.
a.clue: Square each component, add, then take the square root.

b.q: Which is the unit vector in the same direction as \(6i + 8j\)?
b.why: \(|6i + 8j| = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\), so divide each component by 10 to get \(\frac{3}{5}i + \frac{4}{5}j\). Check: \(\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{2} = \frac{9}{25} + \frac{16}{25} = 1\). Dividing by 14, the sum of the components, gives \(\frac{3}{7}i + \frac{4}{7}j\), which has magnitude less than 1.
b.clue: Find the magnitude first, then divide both components by it.
